questions.question: Driving combination vehicles requires ____ skill than driving single vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single vehicles. They need more skill to operate safely.

questions.question: During a trip, landing gear should be:
questions.explanation: Landing gear must always be completely raised before driving. Gear that is not fully raised can catch on railroad tracks or other hazards on the road.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, the ____ trailer should be directly behind the cab.
questions.explanation: The heaviest loaded trailer should be closest to the tractor. The lightest trailer should be at the rear.

questions.question: Trailers with low underneath clearance can present challenges when driving over:
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings can be difficult to cross with low-clearance trailers. Long trailers and single-axle tractors are especially at risk.

questions.question: At speeds under 40 mph, keep at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: During a trip, the ____ should be open.
questions.explanation: All shut-off valves should be open during a trip, except the last valve on the rear trailer. This ensures air reaches all trailer brakes and cannot escape from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used:

options.text: To check the connection between the trailer and tractor.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve applies the trailer brakes and should only be used for testing. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor attached to two trailers

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer. Drivers must exercise caution when operating one.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor that travels faster than the speed limit

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer. These are difficult to operate and drivers must be careful.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second trailer, the trailer height should be ____ the center of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.question: What do shut-off valves do?

options.text: Stop air from leaving the air brake system.
Stop air from entering the air brake system.
Control vehicles that are out of control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop air from leaving the air brake system.
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves control air flow between trailers. Always keep the rear shut-off valve closed to prevent air from leaving the braking system.

questions.question: The service air line is controlled by the foot brake and attached to the ____ valves.
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves, which apply the trailer brakes quickly.

questions.question: When should you use the trailer hand valve for parking?

options.text: Only use it for parking on a downgrade.

questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can release air pressure and cause the brakes to release. Instead, use the parking brake or wheel chocks.

questions.question: When should you look into the back of the fifth wheel?

options.text: If your vehicle begins to skid.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling, go under the trailer and look into the back of the fifth wheel. Make sure the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin shank.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the cab and call for help.
Leave the cab and walk away from the tracks.
Signal another driver to push your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the cab and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave the vehicle immediately and walk away from the tracks. Call emergency services.

questions.question: An empty combination vehicle will have:
questions.explanation: An empty combination vehicle has less weight, so the stiff suspension springs and strong brakes have lower traction than a fully-loaded vehicle.

questions.question: What happens if a trailer is too high?
questions.explanation: Check the trailer height before coupling. A low trailer can damage the nose. A high trailer may not couple correctly.

questions.question: Which trailer is most likely to roll over during a quick turn?
questions.explanation: Turn gently and smoothly. A quick turn while pulling trailers risks rolling over the last trailer.

questions.question: When crossing traffic in a combination vehicle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will make room for your vehicle.
Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space than other vehicles. Always wait for a large enough gap in traffic to cross safely.

questions.question: How do you test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve, charge the air supply, turn off the engine, then press the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to emergency position when pressure drops too low.
